Let S be a surface and Q ⊂S a ﬁnite set of marked points. We denote by Homeo(S, Q) the group of homeomorphisms of S that ﬁx Q as a set and ﬁx the boundary pointwise. The mapping class group of S, seen as a surface with marked points is Mod(S, Q) := π0(Homeo+(S, ∂S) ∩Homeo(S, Q)).

candidates.statement: We have already encountered an important example of a bialgebra, the universal enveloping algebra U(g) of a Lie algebra g. Recall that the coproduct is the unique algebra homomorphism ∆: U(g) →U(g) ⊗U(g), with the property that ∆(x) = 1 ⊗x + x ⊗1, for any x ∈g.
